The answer is most likely D, about 75%. This is from memory of the World Bank's mid-1990s figures, not a lookup. As I recall, low-income countries held roughly 55% of world population and lower-middle-income countries another ~20%, which gives about 75%. I'm unsure about the $1230 cutoff, since it doesn't match the Bank's standard thresholds as I remember them. That mismatch is why my confidence isn't higher.

CONFIDENCE: 55
